---
title: "EcoPhyloSim: model behavior across versions"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    toc: true
execute:
  echo: false
---

This document records how the biological behavior of the model changes between
versions of EcoPhyloSim. Each version is represented by one run of
`PhyloSim/data-raw/packageBehavior.R` (see the vignette chapter "Emerging
patterns" and `?packageBehavior`), archived with `archive.R` and exported with
`addRun.R` to `runs/<version>_<commit>.csv.gz` (the value of each indicator at
the last census of each replicate, the pooled CNDD coefficient and the runtime in
seconds, for every setting of the main run). Behavior that differs from
expectations but is not a bug of the code is noted here; problems of the code go
to issues. Runtimes are comparable only between runs on the same machine.

To add a version: run `packageBehavior.R`, archive the cache with
`Rscript model-behavior/archive.R <cache> <output folder> <version> <commit>`, run
`Rscript model-behavior/addRun.R <archive folder>` from the repository root, add a
section with notes below, and render this file with
`quarto render model-behavior/model-behavior.qmd`. If parameters are renamed or the
design changes, update the definitions of the key settings below.

```{r setup}
files <- list.files("runs", pattern = "\\.csv\\.gz$", full.names = TRUE)
# order versions by version number (file names <version>_<commit>.csv.gz)
files <- files[order(numeric_version(sub("_.*", "", basename(files))))]
reps <- lapply(files, read.csv)
names(reps) <- sub("\\.csv\\.gz$", "", basename(files))
# replicate mean, sd and number of non-missing replicates per setting and indicator
# (missing parameter values as "NA", so that aggregate() keeps their settings)
runs <- lapply(reps, function(d) {
  d <- d[!is.na(d$value), ]
  keys <- setdiff(names(d), c("simulation", "rep", "value"))
  d[keys] <- lapply(d[keys], function(x) if (anyNA(x)) ifelse(is.na(x), "NA", x) else x)
  a <- aggregate(d["value"], d[keys], function(v) c(mean = mean(v), sd = sd(v), n = length(v)))
  data.frame(a[keys], mean = a$value[, "mean"], sd = a$value[, "sd"], n = a$value[, "n"])
})

# key settings: block and parameter values
key <- list(
  "Neutral, global dispersal" = list(block = "neutral", x = 50, specRate = 2),
  "Neutral, dispersal 1 (reference)" = list(block = "dispersal", dispersal = "1"),
  "Environment 1, global" = list(block = "environment", dispersal = "global", environment = 1),
  "Environment 1, dispersal 1" = list(block = "environment", dispersal = "1", environment = 1),
  "Density 1, dispersal 1" = list(block = "density", density = 1, densityCut = 1),
  "Environment 0.5 + density 0.5" = list(block = "envDensity", environment = 0.5, density = 0.5),
  "Environment 1 + density 1, dispersal 1" = list(block = "assembly", dispersal = "1", environment = 1, density = 1),
  "Protracted 1" = list(block = "speciation", protracted = 1, redQueen = 0),
  "Red Queen 0.01 (strength 100)" = list(block = "speciation", redQueen = 0.01))
indicators <- c("richness", "shannon", "conspecificNeighbors", "corTraitEnv",
                "sdCompetitionTrait", "colless", "gamma", "meanSpeciesAge", "cndd", "runtime")

# "mean ± half-width of the 95% confidence interval" of one key setting
fingerprint <- function(d, k) {
  s <- d
  for (n in names(k)) if (n %in% names(s)) s <- s[s[[n]] == k[[n]], ]
  sapply(indicators, function(i) {
    r <- s[s$indicator == i, ]
    if (nrow(r) != 1) return(NA)
    ci <- qt(0.975, pmax(r$n - 1, 1)) * r$sd / sqrt(r$n)
    sprintf("%s ± %s", signif(r$mean, 3), signif(ci, 1))
  })
}
```

## Key settings per version

Replicate mean ± half-width of the 95% confidence interval (indicators at the last
census, CNDD over the last five generations, runtime of the whole simulation in
seconds; 50 × 50 cells, `specRate = 2`, other parameters at their defaults unless
stated).

```{r tables, results = "asis"}
for (v in names(runs)) {
  tab <- t(sapply(key, fingerprint, d = runs[[v]]))
  cat("\n### ", v, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(tab))
  cat("\n")
}
```

```{r compare, eval = length(runs) > 1, results = "asis"}
cat("\n## Changes between the last two versions\n\n")
v <- tail(names(reps), 2)
old <- reps[[v[1]]]
new <- reps[[v[2]]]
# a parameter that exists in only one version: keep only its most frequent value
# there (the default), so that settings are not pooled
for (d in c("old", "new")) {
  x <- get(d)
  for (n in setdiff(names(x), c(names(old), names(new))[duplicated(c(names(old), names(new)))])) {
    if (n %in% c("simulation", "setting", "rep", "generations", "value")) next
    x <- x[x[[n]] %in% names(which.max(table(x[[n]]))), names(x) != n]
  }
  assign(d, x)
}
cols <- setdiff(intersect(names(old), names(new)), c("simulation", "setting", "rep", "generations", "value"))
rowKey <- function(d) do.call(paste, c(d[cols], sep = "\r"))
o <- split(old$value, rowKey(old))
n <- split(new$value, rowKey(new))
both <- setdiff(intersect(names(o), names(n)), grep("\rruntime$", names(o), value = TRUE))
p <- vapply(both, function(k) tryCatch(t.test(o[[k]], n[[k]])$p.value,
                                       error = function(e) NA_real_), numeric(1))
m <- unique(new[cols])[match(both, rowKey(unique(new[cols]))), ]
m$mean.old <- vapply(o[both], mean, numeric(1), na.rm = TRUE)
m$mean.new <- vapply(n[both], mean, numeric(1), na.rm = TRUE)
m$d <- (m$mean.new - m$mean.old) /
  sqrt((vapply(o[both], var, numeric(1), na.rm = TRUE) + vapply(n[both], var, numeric(1), na.rm = TRUE)) / 2)
m$p.adj <- p.adjust(p, "holm")
cat("Comparison of ", v[2], " with ", v[1], ": difference of the replicate means (newer",
    " minus older) for settings with the same parameter values in both runs, where a Welch",
    " test of the replicates is significant after Holm correction over all ", length(both),
    " comparisons (p < 0.05; runtime not tested); d is the difference in units of the pooled",
    " standard deviation. Settings and indicators only in one version: ",
    length(setdiff(union(names(o), names(n)), intersect(names(o), names(n)))), ".\n\n", sep = "")
sig <- which(m$p.adj < 0.05)
shown <- cols[vapply(m[cols], function(x) length(unique(x)) > 1, logical(1))]
if (length(sig)) print(knitr::kable(m[sig, c(shown, "mean.old", "mean.new", "d", "p.adj")],
                                    digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)) else cat("No significant differences.\n")
```

## Notes per version

### 0.3.1, commit 852c61e (before the redesign of density dependence)

Run with commit 852c61e, before the redesign of fitness and density dependence
proposed in #172. Polytomies of the phylogeny were resolved at random (changed
in #174, which changes the Colless index for a given seed). Runs of 50,000
generations (100,000 in the density block, 200,000 in the neutral block).

- Neutral model: richness up to about 15% above the Ewens sampling formula
  (batch speciation, #124); share of conspecific neighbors and rank–abundance
  curve as expected; Colless index and gamma statistic positive.
- Density dependence is weak and saturates already at `density = 0.25`:
  richness increases only from about 20 to 25 species, and the competition
  traits split into two groups at the ends of their range [0, 1] (#133, #144).
- Combined with environmental filtering, density dependence reduces richness.
- The model is neutral if environment and density are both > 0 and their sum is
  ≤ 1 (#144).
- Environmental filtering with global dispersal stays weak (correlation of trait
  and environment 0.24 at `environment = 1`) and becomes even weaker with narrow
  niches; with local dispersal, traits match the environment almost perfectly.
  Filtering does not increase spatial aggregation.
- Filtering makes trees more balanced (Colless index < 0) and increases the
  gamma statistic.
- A Red Queen advantage of 0.01 with strength 100 more than doubles richness and
  reduces the mean species age from about 400 to 20 generations.
- Protracted speciation acts like a speciation rate reduced by exp(-p).
- CNDD estimated from mortality: about 0 in the neutral model, positive with
  density dependence, negative with environmental filtering (strongest with
  global dispersal).
